ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]The AI Kill Chain | Track3-03 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: The AI Kill Chain | Track3-03 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
AI vulnerabilities rarely cause major incidents alone. Impact emerges when weaknesses chain across AI systems, identities, tools, data, and business processes.
This talk introduces the AI Kill Chain through realistic scenarios and a live demo, showing how prompt injection enables tool abuse, poisoned knowledge influences decisions, agent memory creates persistence, and agent trust enables lateral movement. See how least-privilege agents, tool authorization, trust boundaries, human approval, and secure architecture can break the chain.
Leave with a practical methodology to identify, model, and mitigate AI attack chains before they become breaches.
Demo link: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1l53XbHOIM3vhYkwnXsuEc_oDVy8hJAM-/view?usp=sharing

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]One guardrail is not enough: Defense-in-depth against LLM jailbreaks | Track3-02 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: One guardrail is not enough: Defense-in-depth against LLM jailbreaks | Track3-02 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Production chatbots have been talked into binding contracts, creating legal liability, and leaking data through RAG. OWASP ranks prompt injection as the #1 GenAI risk and notes that RAG and fine-tuning do not eliminate it.
This talk presents a defense-in-depth architecture on AWS, reframing jailbreaks as two problems: a universal safety baseline inherited from the model and a bot-specific scope envelope that teams must define. Explore the pipeline: a fine-tuned BERT classifier on SageMaker, moderation and PII filtering, an LLM canonicalizer, hostile-input retrieval, guarded generation, and output filtering. Close the loop with asynchronous LLM-as-judge triage that turns production attacks into training data, continuously strengthening the cheapest defense layer. Demo link :- https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hoaXYTaz6o5WNGe-fyQ3Fz7bGOsu3E3F/view?usp=drive_link

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Human in the loop is not enough | Track3-01 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Human in the loop is not enough | Track3-01 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
"Shipping an AI product is easy; securing it is where teams get caught off guard. We share lessons from building an enterprise AI platform on a third-party foundation model, where human oversight proved insufficient as the platform evolved toward autonomous and agentic capabilities.
Explore practical security lessons across governance, risk, cloud architecture, threat modelling, penetration testing, and guardrails for systems that act, not just respond. See how risks evolved from OWASP Top 10 for web apps to LLM and Agentic Apps."

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]TFM based Shared Intelligence Layer | Track2-03 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: TFM based Shared Intelligence Layer | Track2-03 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Augmenting your existing AI/ML models Every model in a bank sits on its own feature pipeline, compressing the same customer event stream into aggregates that discard ordering and timing. Transaction Foundation Models learn from the sequence instead. This session explores what a shared intelligence layer changes for models already in production, what augmenting existing models involves, and how the NVIDIA stack and blueprint make the build methodical and repeatable. Includes a live demonstration.
Demo link: https://tfmgnndecksite.vercel.app"

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Deep research at scale | Track2-02 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Deep research at scale | Track2-02 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Deep research at scale - Evolving from LangGraph to DeepAgents across 15M+ documents Scaling LLMs to 15M+ domain-heavy documents exposes the limits of standard RAG. Complex enterprise queries demand multi-hop reasoning, multi-document synthesis, and strict domain accuracy.
We share our blueprint for taking a multi-agent deep research engine from prototype to production, covering HPC-based retrieval, the evolution from LangGraph ReAct to DeepAgents, and evaluation using reranking, LLM-as-a-judge, custom rubrics, and human verification. We also share lessons from MLflow observability, streaming logs, and Bedrock infrastructure.
Learn what it takes to reliably bring non-deterministic agentic workflows into production at scale."

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]But it worked in my PoC! | Track2-01 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: But it worked in my PoC! | Track2-01 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description:
"What does it take to automate enterprise IT at scale with AI agents? More than expected. This talk shares the hard-won lessons from deploying agents to manage software updates across thousands of devices globally. Our first attempt collapsed under bloated prompts. The second relied on an all-knowing orchestrator that consumed 80% of its context, took two minutes to respond, burned 3M tokens per run, and hallucinated its way to failure. The third shipped.
Discover what finally worked: smaller agents with tighter responsibilities, on-demand skills, structured agent-to-agent communication, dynamic agent spawning, deterministic workflows, dedicated Q&A, and tool-call validation. Learn why multi-agent systems are a distributed systems problem first and an AI problem second. No theory. Pure scar tissue."

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Engineering the harness | Track1-02 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Engineering the harness | Track1-02 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description: Your AI coding agent isn't the problem, the harness around it is. In "Engineering the Harness," we explore why smart models ignore team conventions, then share a practical system of guides that steer agents before they act and sensors that catch mistakes after. Drawing from a brownfield multi-repo platform and a greenfield agentic workflow, we show how to build a setup that works with any AI tool or stack. Leave with a concrete checklist to audit your team's AI setup. Online presentation link: https://jaya-nandyala-tw.github.io/xconf-engineering-the-harness/deck/s1

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]AI First Legacy Migration | Track1-01 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: AI First Legacy Migration | Track1-01 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description: Explore an agentic orchestration pipeline for large-scale legacy modernisation that shifts the focus from code translation to behavioural reconstruction. Extract language-agnostic specifications covering business rules, data models, architecture, and cross-cutting concerns to deterministically regenerate applications on a new technology stack. Stateful test-driven generation, automated validation, and iterative self-correction ensure behavioural equivalence while reducing migration effort and risk. The process also surfaces undocumented business logic and edge cases, giving teams deeper insight into legacy systems.

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [Thoughtworks]Build an AI knowledge fabric for your organisation | Keynote 2 | Xconf India 2026

ns2:group.ns2:title: Build an AI knowledge fabric for your organisation | Keynote 2 | Xconf India 2026
ns2:group.ns2:description: As organizations adopt autonomous AI agents, context is the critical bottleneck. LLMs have vast world knowledge but lack business insight, leading to hallucinations and latency. Explore how an "AI Knowledge Fabric" can bridge this gap through a dynamic, agent-optimized semantic layer. Discover its three pillars: engineering, industry, and institutional knowledge, plus the rules for formatting, continuous updates, and guardrails. Learn how to turn generic models into specialized digital teammates. Speaker :- Sunit Parekh, CTO, India and Middle East, Thoughtworks

ns0:entry.ns0:title: [MacRumors]iPhone Duo Hands-On: I’m VERY Impressed

ns2:group.ns2:title: iPhone Duo Hands-On: I’m VERY Impressed
ns2:group.ns2:description:
Apple’s first foldable iPhone is finally here. I went hands-on with the brand new iPhone Duo, and after spending some time with Apple’s $1,999 foldable, I’m impressed.
The iPhone Duo features a 7.6-inch folding inner display, 5.4-inch outer display, titanium design, A20 Pro chip, dual 48-megapixel cameras, MagSafe, and an incredibly thin design. Apple has also put a huge amount of work into minimizing the display crease with a new nanotexture finish and redesigned folding display.
But some of the most interesting parts of the iPhone Duo are the software. iOS adapts to the larger folding display, supports two apps side-by-side, introduces new half-folded experiences, and even turns the Duo into a standalone StandBy display without needing to be connected to a charger.
There are still some questions, including the lack of a telephoto camera, limited multitasking controls, long-term hinge durability, and of course that $1,999 starting price.
These are my first impressions after going hands-on with the iPhone Duo. A full review is coming soon, so let me know what you want me to test!
iPhone Duo pre-orders begin October 16, with the official release on October 23.
